page.layout: Running head at top centre-left: "CAP. II: 18-19. ILLUSTRATUS." with page number 501 at top right. One column of running text, full width, with main body in roman and italic. Below the text: signature line "Rrr 3" at centre-left and "SUB-" catchword at right.

main_text.p: imagines fuisse rerum falsarum, suas verarum: Pat-lum ajunt idolum describere, quod nihil esset mundo, quia sita simulacra eorum erant, qui aut nunquam fuerant, aut æternis adjudicati suppliciis, solis ignibus vivunt. Sua autem dicunt Christum & sanctos cœlites referre. Ast quo argumento præstabunt omnes, quos colunt etiam in simulacris, aut fuisse in rerum natura, aut cœlites esse, & non æternis suppliciis immersos? cum de multis haud levis sit dubitatio. Quomodo probant Georgium illum Draconicidam, Christophorum, Catharinam, aliosque, unquam in rerum natura extitisse, & quos Papa canonizavit sanctos, revera gloriam ingressos? num Papa etiam in hac causa falli non potuit? Si non sunt idola, simulacra hominum, qui nunc inter cœlites degunt? forte idolum non est Saturni simulacrum, quem multi viri docti Noachum fuisse existimant: ut jam nihil dicam de Mercurio, Baccho aliisque. Imo idolum nihil esse dicit Apostolus; quia exemplaria eorum non sunt, quod esse repræsentantur: atqui id verum esse de omnibus sanctis & beatâ virgine nos asserimus: repræsentantur enim ut in cœlis certis causis patrocinantes, ac res humanas divisis curis curantes, ut divi divæque: quod falsum esse multis probârunt nostri Theologi: ac proin eorum simulacra idola sunt, quæ colunt. Quod si verum est, terreat illos judicium, quod extat Apoc. 22:15. Foris erunt canes, ... & idolis servientes.

page.notes: Top line is partly cut off at the left edge ("imagines" begins the page as a continuation; the previous line's start is not visible, so the first paragraph is marked as continuing from the previous page). Long s has been normalised to s per the rules, and i/j, u/v spelling was regularised in the Latin. The "Apoc." reference is printed as "Apoc. 22 : 15." and the "Foris erunt canes" line ends with a printed ellipsis. Lower part of the page is blank except for the signature and catchword, and the page is the second of a gathering, so no further text is present. Some words at the top-left edge are partially damaged: "Pat-lum" is printed as "Pattlum" with a break; read as "Pallum" in the source and transcribed here as printed.
